title: Unable to resolve MagicDNS or tailnet FQDN's after macOS DNS behavior changes in OSS tailscaled 1.74.0
body:
### What is the issue?

In OSS `tailscaled` prior to 1.74.0 (last working version 1.72.1), I could resolve MagicDNS _and_ tailnet FQDN's (*.ts.net) under the following setup. The changelog notes changes in this area in 1.74.0: https://tailscale.com/changelog#2024-09-12.

* OSS `tailscaled` running with `--accept-dns=false`
* App Store or Standalone macOS Tailscale app running with "Use Tailscale DNS settings" **off**

After updating OSS `tailscaled` to 1.74.0, I now _must_ turn on Tailscale DNS in the App Store or Standalone Tailscale macOS app to get MagicDNS or tailnet FQDN's to resolve. **Enabling `--accept-dns` on `tailscaled` 1.74.0 does not work to resolve MagicDNS names or tailnet FQDN's**, even with the App Store or Standalone macOS Tailscale app not running.

This is undesirable as I need to use my local network's DNS server, with split DNS handling tailnet FQDN's. [I only turn on Tailscale DNS when using an exit node](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/12641#issue-2378598741).

Please note that `tailscaled` runs as root (`brew services start tailscale`), in case that's relevant.

Output from tailscaled 1.74.0 `dns status` command (with redactions):

<details>
=== 'Use Tailscale DNS' status ===

Tailscale DNS: enabled.

Tailscale is configured to handle DNS queries on this device.
Run 'tailscale set --accept-dns=false' to revert to your system default DNS resolver.

=== MagicDNS configuration ===

This is the DNS configuration provided by the coordination server to this device.

MagicDNS: enabled tailnet-wide (suffix = <redacted-host>)

Other devices in your tailnet can reach this device at REDACTED.

Resolvers (in preference order):
  (no resolvers configured, system default will be used: see 'System DNS configuration' below)

Split DNS Routes:
  - ts.net.                        -> 199.247.155.53
  - ts.net.                        -> 2620:111:8007::53

Search Domains:
  - <redacted-host>

=== System DNS configuration ===

This is the DNS configuration that Tailscale believes your operating system is using.
Tailscale may use this configuration if 'Override Local DNS' is disabled in the admin console,
or if no resolvers are provided by the coordination server.

Nameservers:
  - REDACTED
  - REDACTED
  - REDACTED
  - REDACTED

Search domains:
  - home.arpa

[this is a preliminary version of this command; the output format may change in the future]
</details>

Please let me know what further info can be provided. Thank you!

### Steps to reproduce

_No response_

### Are there any recent changes that introduced the issue?

Updated OSS `tailscaled` (installed via `brew`) to 1.74.0 from 1.72.1

### OS

macOS

### OS version

macOS 14.6.1

### Tailscale version

1.74.0

### Other software

_No response_

### Bug report

BUG-3104a4f350ae354f7eedcc95e4ce78e5b8da482124d9bbdb7feabf0f446a757f-20240913143438Z-a9cd88dd1f260627

comments.body:
Okay, so I am almost certainly wrong that `tailscaled` was ever enabling the resolution of tailnet FQDN's without `--accept-dns=true`. But here's what I found was not working for me in 1.74.0 after reinstalling 1.72.1 and comparing the output of `scutil --dns` across 1.72.1 and 1.74.0.

`sudo brew service start tailscale` (or the equivalent for 1.72.1) is used to run `tailscaled`. I followed these directions approximately to get 1.72.1 reinstalled through `brew`: https://cmichel.io/how-to-install-an-old-package-version-with-brew/ (you'll need to fix the broken formula by commenting out the completions bit in the install block).

In the following configuration, 1.72.1 works as I desire: local DNS servers are hit first, and I can resolve tailnet FQDN's in the browser no problem.

comments.body:
There's a lot going on in this thread and I'm not participant17% sure it's the same issue I'm seeing, but this is what I've found: 

- I recently switched from the package installer GUI app to the CLI via homebrew
- Went the CLI route in order to get tailscale running at boot (before login), particularly on a mac mini which is currently headless
- The CLI does not modify resolv.conf (as [noted on the wiki](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/wiki/Tailscaled-on-macOS#comparison-to-gui-version))
- I believe the wiki falls a little short in describing the DNS change that's needed:

As in this thread, I added `participant17.participant17.participant17.participant17` as the first resolver but ran into issues with being unable to resolve tailnet hosts while other hosts worked fine. When my resolv.conf looks like:

```
search <redacted-host> lan
nameserver participant17.participant17.participant17.participant17
nameserver 1.1.1.1
```

I get the following result:

```
$ host bar
<redacted-host> has address participant17.x.y.z
$ ping bar
ping: cannot resolve bar: Unknown host
```

If I remove `1.1.1.1` from resolv.conf, `ping` succeeds. 

I believe the way the GUI operates is that when tailscaled is `up`, it picks up all nameservers from resolv.conf, ignores `participant17.participant17.participant17.participant17` if it's present and uses the remaining servers as the upstream resolver list. Then it modifies resolv.conf so *only* participant17.participant17.participant17.participant17 is present. In fact, it also appears to do this on my linux server running Ubuntu 22.04 with the following note:

```
# resolv.conf(5) file generated by tailscale
# For more info, see https://tailscale.com/s/resolvconf-overwrite
# DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE BY HAND -- CHANGES WILL BE OVERWRITTEN
```

I think there are a couple of options here - 

1. modify tailscaled so it also updates resolv.conf, just as it does on linux. I'm not sure why this behavior differs between the Mac GUI (and the network extension) vs the CLI, since it already works that way on linux, probably something to do with the mac's funky DNS setup
2. add a config to tailscaled so that we can directly supply it with a list of nameservers for its resolver instead of slurping them from resolv.conf, allowing us to manually make the needed changes and have everything work

I'm currently leaning towards the second option as it seems fairly easy to do and I can get my system working with a couple of changes.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
Found another solution on macOS which is to create a domain-specific resolver file:

```sh
sudo mkdir -p /etc/resolver # if it doesn't exist already
echo "nameserver participant17.participant17.participant17.participant17" | sudo tee /etc/resolver/ts.net
sudo dscacheutil -flushcache
sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
```

This should ensure that only lookups for `*.ts.net` are routed to tailscaled and everything else to the nameservers configured in `resolv.conf`.

Only minor issue I'm seeing is that `host <device>` doesn't work as it only uses `resolv.conf`. See this note:

```
macOS NOTICE
       The host command does not use the host name and address resolution or the DNS query routing mechanisms used by other processes running on macOS.  The results of name or address queries
       printed by host may differ from those found by other processes that use the macOS native name and address resolution mechanisms.  The results of DNS queries may also differ from queries
       that use the macOS DNS routing library.
```

Instead you can use the following utility:

```sh
dns-sd -G v4 <device>
```

comments.author: participant14
comments.body:
Finally resolved related issues, macos 26.3, running tailscale from nixpkgs.

```
$ tailscale --version
1.94.1
  long version: 1.94.1
  go version: go1.25.5
```

I had previously seen multiple files (some related to tailscale) in `/etc/resolver/` and wasn't sure how those were being created, so I renamed the directory.

I found that a round-trip of shutting down tailscale, tailscaled, and relaunching them recreated `/etc/resolver/` and `/etc/resolver/search.tailscale`, but not the other files, and DNS was *not* working for my tailnet (in spite of `dscacheutil -flushcache` and `sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder`).

```console
$ tailscale down
$ sudo launchctl bootout system/com.tailscale.tailscaled
$ sudo launchctl bootstrap system /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.tailscale.tailscaled.plist
$ tailscale up --accept-dns=true
$ dscacheutil -flushcache
$ sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
$ ping <redacted-host>
ping: unknown host
```

Interestingly, I found that deleting `/etc/resolv.conf` as well as `/etc/resolver/` seems to prompt tailscale to regenerate all the files in `/etc/resolver/`.

Further, `/etc/resolv.conf` is just a symlink to `/var/run/resolv.conf`. One can regenerate `/var/run/resolv.conf` by toggling wifi on and off (either via gui or `networksetup -setairportpower en0 on`).

So the only step I haven't figured out is how to provoke regeneration of the `/etc/resolv.conf` symlink, but that's easy enough to do manually: `sudo ln -s /var/run/resolv.conf /etc/`

So, round trip, so you can see at which point each file is recreated and when dns starts working again:

```console
$ tailscale status --json | jq -r .BackendState
Running
$ sudo rm -rf /etc/resolver /etc/resolv.conf /var/run/resolv.conf
$ ls /etc/resolver | wc -l
ls: cannot access '/etc/resolver': No such file or directory
0
$ ping <redacted-host>
ping: unknown host
$ tailscale down
$
$ # /etc/resolver directory has been regenerated but is empty:
$ ls /etc/resolver | wc -l
0
$ tailscale up --accept-dns=true
$
$ # /etc/resolver is now populated and magic DNS is working
$ ls /etc/resolver | wc -l
68
$ ping <redacted-host>
PING <redacted-host> (participant17.X.X.X): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from participant17.X.X.X: icmp_seq=0 ttl=64 time=74.641 ms
$ ls -l /etc/resolv.conf /var/run/resolv.conf
ls: cannot access '/etc/resolv.conf': No such file or directory
ls: cannot access '/var/run/resolv.conf': No such file or directory
$ networksetup -setairportpower en0 off
$
$ # /var/run/resolv.conf has now been recreated but doesn't have any nameservers
$ grep -q nameserver /var/run/resolv.conf
$ echo $?
1
$ networksetup -setairportpower en0 on
$ # /var/run/resolv.conf now has nameservers
$ grep -q nameserver /var/run/resolv.conf
$ echo $?
0
$ ls -l /etc/resolv.conf /var/run/resolv.conf
ls: cannot access '/etc/resolv.conf': No such file or directory
-rw-r--r-- 1 root daemon 334 Feb 28 09:00 /var/run/resolv.conf
$ # recreating /etc/resolv.conf is the last piece of the puzzle
$ sudo ln -s /var/run/resolv.conf /etc/
```
